description: Input-projection ablation of the naive LUT: CompressionMHL with input reprojection ON (inner_in_dim=48) and output compression OFF (inner_out_dim=-1, full-width 384 table rows). H=4, nap=8, tph=128 (R=512). 16k steps under the corrected scaffolding; val curve and final score both use the fixed protocol (bs48x100 skip12, held-out shard_06542 from token 0).

checkpoint_reload_check.note: re-scoring the saved checkpoint reproduces summary.json exactly

comparison: corrected vanilla anchor exp_n_0135 = 1.165147; naive baseline exp_n_0136 = 1.192926. RESULT: input projection alone (no output compression) recovers most of the naive-LUT deficit — this run is -0.0163 BELOW the naive 0136 and only +0.0115 above the corrected vanilla dense baseline, vs 0136's +0.0278 gap. So adding an input reprojection to d_in=48 closes ~59% of the naive LUT's gap to dense, WITHOUT any output compression.
training_stability: clean; monotonic to the end (final [VAL] steps 14500/15000/15500/16000 = 1.1798/1.1784/1.1773/1.1766). No instability.
